messages.content: Help me generate the XContent with xContentBuilderInstance for a RootObjectMapper that includes default settings for dynamic date formats, dynamic templates, date detection, and numeric detection, while skipping runtime fields?

function.name: RootObjectMapper_doXContent
function.description: Serializes the RootObjectMapper settings to XContent, with options to include default values and to skip runtime fields. Note that the provided function is in Java 8 SDK syntax.

builder.description: The XContentBuilder to which the content should be written. This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation.

params.description: Parameters controlling the serialization, including whether to include defaults and whether to skip runtime fields. This is Java ArrayList type parameter in string representation. The list elements are of type any; they are not in string representation.

message.content:
Below is a minimal “recipe” that shows exactly what needs to happen under the hood so that your **RootObjectMapper** ends up serialized into X‑content *with* all the default behaviours enabled (`dynamic_date_formats`, `dynamic_templates`, `date_detection`, `numeric_detection`) **and** with runtime fields explicitly skipped. --- ### 1️⃣ What the caller actually has to do | Step | Code / Tool Call | |------|------------------| | **Create an XContentBuilder** – usually from `XContentFactory`. | ```java
XContentBuilder builder = XContentFactory.jsonBuilder();
``` | | **Build/obtain the RootObjectMapper** – normally you’d get one from the parser when reading a mapping, but for illustration we’ll construct it manually with the default values you asked for. | ```java
// Default values taken straight from ES source code:
String dynamicDateFormats = "strict_date_optional_time|epoch_millis";\nDynamicTemplates dynamicTemplates = Collections.emptyMap();\nboolean dateDetection = true; // enable automatic date detection\nboolean numericDetection= false; // keep the default behaviour (no auto‑detection)\nRootObjectMapper rootMapper = new RootObjectMapper(\n /*name*/null,\n /*mapperTypeName*/Mapper.TypeParser.DEFAULT_TYPE_NAME,\n /*dynamicDateFormat*/dynamicDateFormats,\n /*dynamicTemplate*/dynamicTemplates,\n /*ignoreUnmappedTypes*/false,\n /*dateDetection*/dateDetection,\n /*numericDetection*/numericDetection);\n``` | > ⚠️ If you’re working inside an existing IndexMapping context you probably already own a `RootObjectMapper`; just grab it instead of constructing a brand‑new one. | **Serialize it** – now comes the magic line that tells the serializer to write out *defaults* AND to *omit* runtime fields. | ```java
ArrayList
